### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via listRequests (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService), /api/v1/approvals/requests (route, the route ledger binds it to client method approvals.listRequests))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), /api/v1/approvals/requests (route, the route ledger binds it to client method approvals.listRequests))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/approvals/requests (route, the route ledger binds it to client method approvals.listRequests))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via bindApprovalLockHook (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via listRequests (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via listRequests (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1623977b65b76b404a3a86d7df7833ece18bafb8` — the merge of head `c5115facf00ce3b6047053b9f5630d32a80d6c70` into base `e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1623977b65b76b404a3a86d7df7833ece18bafb8 && git checkout 1623977b65b76b404a3a86d7df7833ece18bafb8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d c5115facf00ce3b6047053b9f5630d32a80d6c70 && git checkout -B drift-repro e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d && git merge --no-ff c5115facf00ce3b6047053b9f5630d32a80d6c70

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c5115facf00ce3b6047053b9f5630d32a80d6c70`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23618 (body and all three comments: triage `6185528133`, claim `6186058217`, os-dev-report `6187170508`); PR #23629 body, its 8-file list and the net diff against `main` at the head (merge-base `72329942f9`, +638/-45); the 39 check-runs on the head, latest per name; `payload-redaction.ts`'s header (#10749) on the head; PR #23614's contract record (`6185049769`); #7497 ruling C (`6051659422`); triage ruling `6185594767` on #23556. Function level only, per the card's security gate.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.**

1. **Row 1: every `payload_display` target title is now picked from the TARGET record as served to the reader.** `enrichRows` filters the referenced objects by the exposure gate first (`servesPayloadDisplayTarget`), asks `servedFields(targets, context, served)` for exactly those, then titles each through `titlesAsServed(object, ids, served.get(object), refTitles)`. **Right.** This is the #10749 header's rule ("applied at SERVE time, keyed on the reading caller") asked of the second object, through the same seam (`resolveReadableSnapshotFields`: readable intersected with not-masked, #20964) and the same pick (`redactSnapshot` then `pickTitle`). A refused target is neither asked nor read, as before. Map keys agree: subjects are keyed `String(object_name)`, targets by the lookup's `reference` string, `byObject` groups rows with a truthy `object_name`; a target that is also a subject object reuses the subject's answer (`served.has(object)`), so one read asks once per object.
2. **`titlesAsServed` is the one title pick for subject and targets.** `resolveSubjectDisplays` now calls it with the subject's served answer; its semantics are byte-equal to the pre-change subject pick (`readable === undefined` serves the whole record, else the redacted one; then `pickTitle`), each caller keeps its own best-effort catch. **Right** under route-and-surface rule 1: one owner, so the subject's `record_title` and the targets' `payload_display` cannot drift.
3. **`servedFields` extracted from `servedSubjectFields`**, which is now a thin wrapper. **Right.** Target keys are added to `served` after `redactPayloads` has run and nothing reads the map after `enrichRows`, so the snapshot redaction is unchanged.
4. **(1) Does any production path still serve a `payload_display` target title from a field the reader may not be served?** On the head I find none. `payload_display` is set in exactly one place (`enrichRows`), reached only from `listRequests` and `loadRequest`, both of which ask the served map with the reading caller's context. The one request read under the system context (`resolveActionToken`, via `getRequest(id, SYSTEM_CTX)`) yields a row whose titles are whole (plugin-security's `isSystem` bypass), but its only consumers are `peekActionToken` and `redeemActionToken`, called by `handleActionPage` and the plugin's self-hosted mount, both HTML through `action-link-pages.ts`, which reads `submitter_name`, `submitter_id`, `step_label`, `record_id`, `process_name`, `process_label`, `object_name`, `object_label` and `current_step` and never `payload` or `payload_display` (as PR #23614's record found at item 7; unchanged by this diff).
5. **Row 2: the `RECORD_LOCKED` sentence picks its title from `ctx.previous` as served to the writer.** `recordTitleOf` has one call site; `asServed` is `redactSnapshot(record, served).payload` when `served` is a list, else the pre-image whole. **Right.** The card's row 2 asked for a measurement first; the report gives one (the real `SecurityPlugin` composed, a writer withholding the display field told its value on the base), which matches the source: `readUpdatePriorRow` is a raw driver read shaped to the declared columns, and plugin-security's grep shows nothing that narrows `previous`. The degradation stays the label-only sentence, the `title === recordId` and `field === 'id'` guards in `recordTitleOf` still hold, so the id never returns; `lockedError` still spells `RECORD_LOCKED` and 409. The three operator sites (the cap on a named-id write, the cap on a predicate write, the unanswerable intersection) name the object's API name only and are untouched.
6. **(3) Row 2's authority.** `writerEnvelope` is `ctx.input.options.context` minus the `__` keys, copied by `withoutOperationPrivateKeys`. I traced it against the engine and the middleware: objectql's `update()` builds `opCtx` with `options` and `context: options?.context`; `executeWithMiddleware(opCtx, …)` hands that object to plugin-security's middleware, which reads `const sc = opCtx.context` and stamps `sc.__writeScope` (and the delegator halves) IN PLACE, never assigning `opCtx.context` anew; the by-id hook context carries `input: { id, data, options: opCtx.options }`, and the predicate path's per-row contexts spread that batch context with the same `options` and a per-row `previous`. So on both write shapes `input.options.context` is, by reference, the envelope the security middleware judged the write by; the strip removes only the sharing-depth stamps, which the FLS projection does not read (`resolveProjectionFieldMask` reads `isSystem`, the permission sets resolved for the context, the object's posture and `onBehalfOf`), and the copy keeps the callee from writing back into the operation. `buildSession` projects `userId`, `organizationId`, `positions`, `accessToken`, `isSystem`, `actor` and the flags, dropping `permissions`, `posture` and `onBehalfOf`, so asking with the session would be the second derivation the change refuses. **Right: the same envelope, derived once.** The pin (c) asserts the envelope carries the writer's `permissions`.
7. **(2) Nothing is granted, and the `undefined` posture is the redaction's on both rows.** Row 1: the target read itself (`engine.find` under `SYSTEM_CTX`) is unchanged; what is served is a subset of what was served before for every reader; the exposure gate (#22738) still runs first. Row 2: no read is added, the refusal set (`gatingRequests`) is untouched; only the sentence's title narrows. Both rows read one seam, so the three fail-open answers (no security service, no object name, a read projection that throws or answers `undefined`) and the one fail-closed answer (`[]`, no title) are identical to the snapshot's; `redactSnapshot(x, undefined)` returns `x` in all three places. In production both rows are fed by the same lazy `fieldVisibility` getter in `approvals-plugin.ts` (row 1 through `attachFieldVisibility`, row 2 passed to the hook, the redaction middleware and the predicate guard receiving the same getter), so an absent security plugin serves every title exactly as before. One case the inbox never reaches and the hook can: a write carrying no envelope asks with `context === undefined`; plugin-security then resolves no set for it and falls through to the object's posture and mask, answering a list or `[]`, so the title narrows or is withheld and never widens past the raw pre-image. The PR's acceptance note names it. **Right.**
8. **The `approvals-plugin.ts` wiring line is within the claim's purpose.** Route-and-surface rule 2: a hook gets its authority because its host mounts it. The only production binder of `bindApprovalLockHook` is this one line; it hands the lock hook the same lazily resolved authority the snapshot redaction already reads; without it row 2's fix would be dead in the composed runtime. **Right**, and declared in the PR body and the report.
9. **`bindApprovalLockHook`'s new optional third parameter.** `lifecycle-hooks.ts` is not exported from `index.ts` and the package's `exports` map is `.` only, so this is a private surface. **Right.**
10. **`nameSubjectRecord`'s comment.** Two comment lines, return value unchanged, the wording triage ruling `6185594767` asked for ("rides the next touch of that file"). **Right.**
11. **Test accept-set changes.** The two pass-through tests pass `new Map()` and a user context to `enrichRows` with no field-visibility source attached, which is the seam's no-service pass-through: what those pins measure. **Right.** New pins: row 1 (a) single read and list, including a self-lookup narrowed by the subject's answer and the stored id standing in the snapshot; (a-masked); (b) control; (c) a withheld display field lends nothing and a title-eligible field the reader may read still names the record, the same declared narrowing PR #23614's record accepted at pin f and the changeset names; (d) one ask per object per read, subject and targets together, on the single read and a multi-row list. Row 2 (a) by-id and predicate; (a-masked); (b) control; (c) one ask per refusal carrying the writer's `permissions`, and none for a write the lock does not refuse; `RECORD_LOCKED` and 409 on every refusal. Both files drive the real service or the real hook on a real engine over sqlite with a field-visibility source giving the contract's three answers. Red-before (8 failed / 2 passed, the two controls) and three restore-proven ablations with predicted sets equal to observed are reported; not re-run here. Not measured: row 1 with `plugin-security` composed; the PR says so.

**Check-runs on the head, as read (latest per name, 39 runs):** 33 completed success, among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, every Lint family, every Type Check family, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core (5/6) and (6/6), the claim and single-writer guards; 6 skipped by design (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood matrix shard, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance). **In progress at read time: Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6).** None failed. The queue's "every check green" condition is the seat's to read at landing time; this verdict is on the contract.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/23618-approval-title-family-served-fields.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` **patch**. **Matches the diff.** The package name matches `package.json`. Nothing published moves: no `packages/spec` file is touched; `ApprovalRequestRow.payload_display` is already optional on the contract (`payload_display?`, a string-to-string record), so an absent key is within the declared shape; `enrichRows`, `servedFields`, `servedSubjectFields`, `titlesAsServed` and `resolveSubjectDisplays` are private; `bindApprovalLockHook` is package-private (judgment 9) and its new parameter optional; `RECORD_LOCKED` and 409 are unchanged; no route, query parameter, translation key, export or notification field changes. A narrowing of served values is patch. `skip-changeset` does not apply and was not used.

`Clause-②: no` is on the PR body, the changeset and the claim, and all three agree with the diff: no published schema or public surface is declared or changed. Right.

Governed surfaces: none in the 8-file list (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`). The Governed Surface Queue Guard is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.

**Deviation 1** (push order: pins, fix and changeset in one push after the empty-branch probe). Answered: the card's security rule that nothing red lands on the remote before the fix governs; no contract effect.

**Deviation 2** (file surface beyond the claim's two sources and their tests). Answered: the `approvals-plugin.ts` line is within purpose (judgment 8); the two pass-through test files are tests of the claimed source, inside the claim's "and their tests", each named in the PR body with its reason. Within surface.

**Deviation 3** (the bounded comment change in `nameSubjectRecord`). Answered: ordered by triage ruling `6185594767`, no behaviour change, correctly without a test or changeset line of its own (judgment 10).

**Deviation 4** (model-free commit trailers and the repository's session footer). Answered: a process note with no contract effect; the repository's instructions govern the seat.

**Deviation 5** (a throwaway measurement file in `plugin-security`'s tree, run once and deleted). Answered: the net diff carries no `plugin-security` path, so nothing of it ships; the measurement is what the card's row 2 asked for first ("measure first"), and its finding (the pre-image is raw; the leak is reachable with the real security plugin) agrees with the source read here (judgment 5).

**Deviation 6** (merged `origin/main` `72329942f9` before opening). Answered: the merge-base of the head against `main` is that commit and the net diff is the 8 files; no contract effect.

**`out_of_scope_findings` entry (4): a `payload_display` lookup target is still read under the system context, so its title is not narrowed by the reader's row-level or sharing access to the target record, only by its declared exposure (#22738) and now by field-level security.** Judged: **a separate question, not a defect this card names; the PR is complete on the card's terms.** The reason, at function level: the card's row 1 names the defect as the reader's field-level security on the target's display field and its done line as the served-fields rule applied to the target object, which this diff does; #23594's class is a title resolved under the system context and served past the caller's FIELD-level security, and row-level access is not in that class. #7497 ruling C fixes what the approval already gives an approver (the inbox entry, the request detail with the snapshot redacted by field-level security, the actions) and keeps record access with object permissions, sharing and row-level rules as a separate authority, consulted for the record, not for what the request itself shows; the #10749 header says the seam deliberately does not gate on object-level access, because an approver routinely has no read on the subject at all. A referenced record's title is derived from the snapshot's key the way the subject's title is, so narrowing it by the reader's row-level or sharing access to the target would be the first approval-path serve that consults record access: a design decision beside ruling C, the same shape PR #23614's record left to a card of its own for the subject (its "assumption 4"), not something this card's text asks for. Nothing moves there in this diff, so it is neither a grant nor a leak this PR introduces. The seat decides any filing.

Reviewed-by: `session_017WLmd5in9RXu7AjyHR8fKQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
